Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-108", "title": "Smoking", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "There's no way around it; smoking is bad for your health."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It harms nearly every organ of the body, even some that you would not expect."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Cigarette smoking causes many cancers and other health problems."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "It is also the cause of nearly one in five deaths in the United States."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Some of the many health problems that smoking can cause include: Cancers."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Smoking is the most common cause of lung and oral cancers."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "But it can also cause cancer in many other parts of your body, such as in your larynx (voice box), esophagus , throat , bladder , kidney , liver , stomach , pancreas , colon and rectum , and cervix ."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "It can also cause acute myeloid leukemia (AML)."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Smoking is the most common cause of COPD ."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "It can also worsen asthma and raise your risk of pneumonia ."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Smoking can damage your blood vessels and make them thicken and grow narrower."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "This makes your heart beat faster and raises your blood pressure ."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Smoking also increases your risk of blood clots and stroke ."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Smoking can raise your risk of cataracts and cause macular degeneration (AMD)."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "You have a greater chance of certain pregnancy problems if you smoke while pregnant ."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Your baby is also at higher risk of dying of sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS)."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Smoking also causes addiction to nicotine, a stimulant drug that is in tobacco."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Nicotine addiction makes it much harder for people to quit smoking ."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "What are the health risks of secondhand smoke?"}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Your smoke is also bad for other people."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "If they breathe in your secondhand smoke , they can get many of the same problems as smokers do."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "These problems can include heart disease and lung cancer."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Children exposed to secondhand smoke have a higher risk of ear infections , colds , pneumonia, bronchitis, and more severe asthma ."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "If you breathe secondhand smoke while pregnant, you're more likely to have preterm labor and a baby with low birth weight ."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Are other forms of tobacco also dangerous?"}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Besides cigarettes, there are several other forms of tobacco."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "Some people smoke tobacco in cigars and water pipes (hookahs)."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "These forms of tobacco also contain harmful chemicals and nicotine."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "Some cigars contain as much tobacco as an entire pack of cigarettes."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "E-cigarettes often look like cigarettes, but they work differently."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "They are battery-operated smoking devices."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "Researchers still have a lot to learn about the health effects of using e-cigarettes."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "We do know that they contain nicotine, which is highly addictive and a health danger to you and your fetus if you are pregnant, children, and teens."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "And e-cigarettes also expose non-smokers to secondhand aerosols (rather than secondhand smoke), which contain harmful chemicals."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "Smokeless tobacco , such as chewing tobacco and snuff, is also bad for your health."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "Smokeless tobacco can cause certain cancers, including oral cancer."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "It also increases your risk of getting heart disease, gum disease , and oral lesions."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Remember, there is no safe level of tobacco use."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "Smoking even just one cigarette per day over a lifetime can cause smoking-related cancers and premature death."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "Quitting smoking can reduce your risk of health problems and add years to your life."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "The earlier you quit, the greater the benefit."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "Some immediate benefits of quitting include: Lower heart rate and blood pressure Less carbon monoxide in the blood (carbon monoxide reduces the blood's ability to carry oxygen) Better circulation Less coughing and wheezing Quitting smoking can be challenging, but it is so important for your health."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "Contact your health care provider if you need help quitting."}]}, {"id": "MLP-3172", "title": "Water Pollution", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "People need it to grow crops and to operate factories, and for drinking and recreation."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Fish and wildlife depend on it to survive."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Many different pollutants can harm our rivers, streams, lakes, and oceans."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "The three most common are soil, nutrients, and bacteria."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Rain washes soil into streams and rivers."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "The soil can kill tiny animals and fish eggs."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "It can clog the gills of fish and block light, causing plants to die."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Nutrients, often from fertilizers, cause problems in lakes, ponds, and reservoirs."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Nitrogen and phosphorus make algae grow and can turn water green."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Bacteria, often from sewage spills, can pollute fresh or salt water."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "You can help protect your water supply: Don't pour household products such as cleansers, beauty products, medicines, auto fluids, paint, and lawn care products down the drain."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Take them to a hazardous waste collection site."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Throw away excess household grease (meat fats, lard, cooking oil, shortening, butter, margarine, etc.) diapers, condoms, and personal hygiene products in the garbage can."}]}, {"id": "MLP-217", "title": "Down Syndrome", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Down syndrome is a condition in which a person has an extra chromosome or an extra piece of a chromosome."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "This extra copy changes how a baby's body and brain develop."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "It can cause both mental and physical challenges during their lifetime."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Even though people with Down syndrome might act and look similar, each person has different abilities."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Chromosomes are tiny \"packages\" in your cells that contain your genes."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Genes carry information, called DNA, that controls what you look like and how your body works."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "People with Down syndrome have an extra copy of chromosome 21."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "In some cases, they may have an extra copy of part of the chromosome."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Having an extra copy of a chromosome is called trisomy."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "So sometimes Down syndrome is also called trisomy 21."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "It happens by chance, as an error when cells are dividing during early development of the fetus ."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "It is not known for sure why Down syndrome occurs or how many different factors play a role."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "One factor that increases the risk of having a baby with Down syndrome is the age of the mother."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Women ages 35 and older are more likely to have a baby with Down syndrome."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "The symptoms of Down syndrome are different in each person."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "And people with Down syndrome may have different problems at different times of their lives."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "They usually have mild to moderate intellectual disabilities."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "For example, they may start talking later than other children."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Some of the common physical signs of Down syndrome include: A flat face Eyes that slant up A short neck Small hands and feet Poor muscle tone Loose joints What other problems does Down syndrome cause?"}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Many people with Down syndrome have the common physical signs and have healthy lives."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "But some people with Down syndrome might have one or more birth defects or other health problems."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Some of the more common ones include: Hearing loss Sleep apnea (a disorder that causes you to repeatedly stop breathing during sleep) Ear infections Eye diseases Congenital heart defects (heart defects that are present at birth) Digestive problems Problems with the upper part of the spine Obesity How is Down syndrome diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Health care providers can check for Down syndrome during pregnancy or after a child is born."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "There are two basic types of tests that help find Down syndrome during pregnancy : Prenatal screening tests can show whether your unborn baby has a higher or lower chance of having Down syndrome."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "If a screening test shows that your baby could have Down syndrome, you'll need another test to find out for sure."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Prenatal diagnostic tests can diagnose or rule out Down syndrome by checking the chromosomes in a sample of cells."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "These tests have a small risk of causing a miscarriage, so they're often done after a screening test shows that an unborn baby could have Down syndrome."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "After a baby is born, the provider may make an initial diagnosis of Down syndrome based on the physical signs of the syndrome."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "The provider can use a karyotype genetic test to confirm the diagnosis."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "The test can check for extra chromosomes in a sample of the baby's blood."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "What are the treatments for Down syndrome?"}, {"id": "S031", "text": "There is no single, standard treatment for Down syndrome."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Treatments are based on each person's physical and intellectual needs, strengths, and limitations."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Services early in life focus on helping children with Down syndrome develop to their full potential."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "These services include speech, occupational, and physical therapies."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "They are typically offered through early intervention programs in each state."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Children with Down syndrome may also need extra help or attention in school, although many children are included in regular classes."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Since people with Down syndrome can have birth defects and other health problems, they will need regular medical care."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "They may need to have certain extra health screenings to check for problems that happen more often in people with Down syndrome."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}, {"id": "MLP-388", "title": "Salivary Gland Disorders", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "You have three pairs of major salivary glands and hundreds of small (minor) glands."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "They make saliva (spit) and empty it into your mouth through openings called ducts."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Saliva makes your food moist, which helps you chew and swallow."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "It also cleans your mouth and contains antibodies that can kill germs."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Problems with salivary glands can cause them to become irritated and swollen."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "You may have symptoms such as: A bad taste in your mouth Difficulty opening your mouth Dry mouth Pain in your face or mouth Swelling of your face or neck Causes of salivary gland problems include infections, obstruction, or cancer ."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Problems can also be due to other disorders, such as mumps or Sjogren's syndrome ."}]}, {"id": "MLP-3797", "title": "Coping with Disasters", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "No matter how well you have prepared , you might feel dazed or numb after going through a disaster."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "You may also feel sad, helpless, or anxious."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "In spite of the tragedy, you might just feel happy to be alive."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "It is not unusual to have bad memories or dreams."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "You may avoid places or people that remind you of the disaster."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "You might have trouble sleeping, eating, or paying attention."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Many people have short tempers and get angry easily."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "These are all normal reactions to stress ."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Sometimes the stress can be too much to handle alone."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Some people have long-term problems after a disaster, including: Post-traumatic stress disorder Depression Self-blame Suicidal thoughts Alcohol or drug misuse If your emotional reactions are getting in the way of your relationships, work, or other important activities, talk to a counselor or your health care provider."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}]
